Lesson · 22 min

Preparing Patients and Examination Rooms

Set up rooms and position patients for examinations and procedures, with attention to safety, dignity, and efficiency.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Prepare an examination room between patients
  • ✓Position patients correctly for common examinations
  • ✓Drape and gown patients to preserve dignity
  • ✓Identify safety risks in the examination room
📘 Reading Lesson

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Preparation is patient care

On the job

You turn over exam rooms at Lakeside Medical Associates.

The provider enters to find the previous patient's table paper still down, the instrument needed for the procedure in another room, and a patient positioned wrongly for the examination. The visit takes twelve minutes longer, and the patient spent five of them in an uncomfortable position for no reason.

Your task: Prepare rooms and patients so the clinical work can happen without interruption.

Position the patient as late as possible, particularly for lithotomy and Sims. These positions are uncomfortable and expose the patient, and leaving someone in one while waiting for the provider is a genuine and avoidable indignity. Drape so that only the area being examined is uncovered, and adjust the drape rather than the patient when possible.
Disinfectants have a required wet contact time — often several minutes — during which the surface must remain visibly wet to be effective. Wiping a surface and immediately drying it does not disinfect it; it cleans it. Read the product label, because the time varies by product and by organism.
Check your understanding

When should a patient be placed in the lithotomy position?

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Room preparation is a sequence worth internalizing.

  1. Write a room turnover checklist in order, from the moment the previous patient leaves to the moment the next is roomed.
  2. For each position in the table, sketch or describe it and name one examination it supports.
  3. Find the label of any hospital-grade disinfectant and note its required wet contact time and the organisms it claims against.
  4. List four safety risks in an examination room and one control for each.
